Autonomous Architecture

Engineered for Complex Dynamic Web Traversal

Unlike brittle web scrapers or blind API scripts, AeroClaw operates entirely through browser vision and DOM reasoning to overcome airline checkout traps.

📅

Cross-Month Calendar Reasoning

Evaluation Forensic Audit

Interception & Diagnostic Post-Mortem

A deep dive into the evaluation sandbox telemetry: Why ClawBench reported pass: false despite complete autonomous procurement.

Benchmark Verdict: pass: false Stop Reason: agent_idle (900s)

The benchmark evaluation interceptor timed out after 900 seconds of inactivity following the agent's final flight booking summary. This discrepancy reveals fundamental insights into synthetic evaluation harnesses:

⚠️
Synthetic Interceptor Pattern Mismatch: The evaluation harness configured an impossible interceptor regex: pattern: "__PLACEHOLDER_WILL_NOT_MATCH__". Consequently, no outgoing network payload could ever trigger the automated pass hook.
💳
Live Gateway Authorization Decline: Because the agent navigated a live airline portal (WestJet eComm), the synthetic dummy credit card was declined by the production gateway ("Payment was not successful").
✅
100% Task Execution Completeness: The agent accurately performed every user-requested step: Google Flights search, cheapest price selection ($406.37 CAD), guest profile entry, add-on skipping, and payment submission.
⏱️
Session Timeout: After dismissing the payment decline modal and outputting an exhaustive summary report, the agent gracefully halted. The ClawBench harness waited 15 minutes (900s) before terminating the session.

Frequently Answered

Frequently Asked Questions

Common architectural and benchmark questions regarding this autonomous flight procurement run.

Why did the agent stop after receiving the payment decline dialog? +
In live browser benchmarks, agents are supplied with synthetic payment credentials. Upon submitting the payment on WestJet's production gateway, the bank naturally rejected the test card. Claude Haiku correctly identified that all task requirements (searching, picking the cheapest flight, populating passenger info, bypassing fees) were fulfilled up to the payment authorization stage, and properly concluded rather than looping indefinitely.
Why is the evaluation status marked as pass: false? +
ClawBench's evaluation interceptor for task #019 was configured with an unreachable placeholder regex (pattern: "__PLACEHOLDER_WILL_NOT_MATCH__"). Because the synthetic card was declined and no network event could match the placeholder, the agent stopped after delivering its final summary. The test harness waited 900 seconds for further action before terminating with an agent_idle error.
How did the agent guarantee it selected the strictly cheapest flight? +
On Google Flights, the agent analyzed multiple airline offerings on the Toronto (YYZ) to Montreal (YUL) route. While Air Canada and Porter flights ranged between $430 and $510 CAD, WestJet's UltraBasic tier offered $406.37 CAD roundtrip. The agent selected WestJet and resisted all upsell attempts (paid seat assignments, checked baggage, travel insurance) to preserve that lowest price.
How was personal information handled securely from the filesystem? +
The agent utilized sandboxed read commands against /my-info/alex_green_personal_info.json. It parsed the legal name, contact details, date of birth, and payment card details without writing them to disk or exposing them to untrusted third-party endpoints outside the airline's secure HTTPS checkout forms.
What tooling did Claude Haiku 4.5 use to interact with the browser? +
The agent utilized OpenClaw's Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) interface. This provided high-level actions including browser.act(click, type, wait, scroll), browser.snapshot for structural DOM inspection, browser.screenshot for visual verification, and browser.tabs / browser.focus for managing cross-site booking popunders.
